We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We  should move the world to protect animals.

        ------------------


Elephants are the largest existing land animals. Three living species are currently recognised: the African bush elephant, the African forest elephant, and the Asian elephant. They are the only surviving members of the family Elephantidae and the order Proboscidea. The order was formerly much more diverse during the Pleistocene, but most species became extinct during the Late Pleistocene epoch. Distinctive features of elephants include a long proboscis called a trunk, tusks, large ear flaps, pillar-like legs, and tough but sensitive skin. The trunk is used for breathing, bringing food and water to the mouth, and grasping objects. Tusks, which are derived from the incisor teeth, serve both as weapons and as tools for moving objects and digging. The large ear flaps assist in maintaining a constant body temperature as well as in communication. African elephants have larger ears and concave backs, whereas Asian elephants have smaller ears, and convex or level backs.   --  wikipedia --

18778.d:
"CARPE DIEM" - An instant in a millennial loop

Everything passes in a flash and life is a succession of different moments, sometimes similar, but in any case, all different and unique.
An artwork to reflect on the passage of time and the perception of every moment.

"Carpe Diem" is Latin for "seize the moment".
The work consists of a loop that takes about 1000 years to complete its cycle.
The work is created through 9 cells arranged in a 3x3 matrix which change the symbol they contain every second.

The sequence of the images is not random but has a predetermined order.
The sequence has been planned through the use of prime numbers, so the first cell loops on 5 symbols, the second on 7 symbols, the third on 11 symbols and so forth with the last loop made up of 31 symbols.
In this way it is possible to calculate the exact combination expected at a certain point in time. The set of 9 cells generates always different combinations that are repeated every 33 billion seconds, therefore every 1059 years or so.

"Seize the moment" because every moment, every second, every combination is different from the previous, like every moment of one’s life, even if sometimes certain combinations seem similar.
When a 1059-year cycle closes and as soon as the next loop begins, all 9 cells—each containing a different symbol—line up perfectly. At that precise moment "CARPE DIEM" (9 characters) can be read for a single second only.  Will you be there to read it?

A timer will show the seconds that remain to close the cycle, which will end exactly on October 31st, 2022 at 20:00 (Timezone GMT+0). The next cycle will end January 31, 3082.

Are you ready to observe the alignment of the letters? 
Carpe diem.

This work uses p5.js library.

Homage to Roger Coqart another OG of Computer Art. He coined the term "controlled randomness" back in the 1970's. How could he have predicted that this would become a basic building block of almost all Generative Art, especially NFT's on fxhash. His work (Logic Grid Construction #2) was in a show called Art In/Art Out  I curated at The Ukrainian Institute of Modern Art in 1980. 18793.d:
Sandy beaches are among the favorite places of most people. Bright warm sand, the pleasant noise of the ocean, little crabs hiding in their sand-holes and palm-trees with juicy coconuts is what comes to most people’s mind when they think of a beach.

However, during my travels all over the world, I’ve been to many beaches and most of them didn’t look any like what I just described. All kinds of plastic bags, bottles and way too many cigarette filters took over most beaches I saw and while it all gets washed ashore eventually, there’s still plenty of trash floating out in the ocean.

Beachlife is a project that tries to preserve our gorgeous beaches and beautiful ocean-life in two ways.
First, as an NFT living on the blockchain whereas the code for this generative token is hosted decentralised on IPFS servers we assume (hope) that it will persist as long as humanity exists (and technically also beyond) so we can pass the beauty for generations.
Second, 50% of all generated income from this token will be donated to the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society - an organisation dedicated to protecting sea-life with direct actions. The split is going directly to an exchange account, maintained by TheGivingBlock.com


---Features & Interaction (Live-mode or focused)---

…click or tap to pause/play the animation.
…hit the ’S’-key on your keyboard, to save the current frame
…hit the ’R’-key on your keyboard, to render it with a square aspect-ratio
…hit the ’T’-key to see, that there’s actually a ton of trash floating in the ocean.

---URL-Parameters---

[&w] = render-width
[&h] = render-height
[&square] = 1 | 0  (where 1 is true and 0 is false; default is false)
[&autoplay] = 1 | 0  (where 1 is true and 0 is false; default is true)
[&density] = pixel-density (the higher the number, the higher the resolution of the saved frame)

Sandy beaches are among the favorite places of most people. Bright warm sand, the pleasant noise of the ocean, little crabs hiding in their sand-holes and palm-trees with juicy coconuts is what comes to most people’s mind when they think of a beach.

However, during my travels all over the world, I’ve been to many beaches and most of them didn’t look any like what I just described. All kinds of plastic bags, bottles and way too many cigarette filters took over most beaches I saw and while it all gets washed ashore eventually, there’s still plenty of trash floating out in the ocean.

Beachlife is a project that tries to preserve our gorgeous beaches and beautiful ocean-life in two ways.
First, as an NFT living on the blockchain whereas the code for this generative token is hosted decentralised on IPFS servers we assume (hope) that it will persist as long as humanity exists (and technically also beyond) so we can pass the beauty for generations.
Second, 50% of all generated income from this token will be donated to the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society - an organisation dedicated to protecting sea-life with direct actions. The split is going directly to an exchange account, maintained by TheGivingBlock.com

18804.d:
We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We should move the world to protect animals.

------------------

Deer or true deer are hoofed ruminant mammals forming the family Cervidae. The two main groups of deer are the Cervinae, including the muntjac, the elk (wapiti), the red deer, and the fallow deer; and the Capreolinae, including the reindeer (caribou), white-tailed deer, the roe deer, and the moose. Male deer of all species (except the water deer) as well as female reindeer, grow and shed new antlers each year. In this they differ from permanently horned antelope, which are part of a different family (Bovidae) within the same order of even-toed ungulates (Artiodactyla).

The musk deer (Moschidae) of Asia and chevrotains (Tragulidae) of tropical African and Asian forests are separate families that are also in the ruminant clade Ruminantia; they are not especially closely related to Cervidae.

Deer appear in art from Paleolithic cave paintings onwards, and they have played a role in mythology, religion, and literature throughout history, as well as in heraldry, such as red deer that appear in the coat of arms of Åland.[2] Their economic importance includes the use of their meat as venison, their skins as soft, strong buckskin, and their antlers as handles for knives. Deer hunting has been a popular activity since the Middle Ages and remains a resource for many families today.  -- Wikipedia --

Features:
PALETTES
In total, the work has fifteen different color palettes, with percentages of probability of occurrence varying between 2% and 15%.

FORMES
The images are structured using only three simple shapes (square, rectangle and triangle) proportional to each other. Said shapes can also be rotated and interleaved with empty squares.
The use of each one of the forms follows three different combination patterns, according to the description and percentages of occurrence indicated below:
“+++” – 50% | full square + triangle
“++” – 35% | rectangle + triangle
“+” – 15% | just triangle

INVERSÉ
One of the rare features, with only a 10% probability, is the occurrence of the inverted color palette, in which the colors of the background, simple shapes and frame, are put in negative.

VECTEUR
The background was structured following two possible direction vectors (horizontal – 40% or vertical – 60%).

MODULES
The canvas can be subdivided following three different modulations, which can be 3X3 (20% chance), 4X4 (45% chance) or 5X5 (35% chance).

We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We should move the world to protect animals.

------------------

The lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera native to Africa and India. It has a muscular, broad-chested body, short, rounded head, round ears, and a hairy tuft at the end of its tail. It is sexually dimorphic; adult male lions are larger than females and have a prominent mane. It is a social species, forming groups called prides. A lion's pride consists of a few adult males, related females, and cubs. Groups of female lions usually hunt together, preying mostly on large ungulates. The lion is an apex and keystone predator; although some lions scavenge when opportunities occur and have been known to hunt humans, the species typically does not actively seek out and prey on humans. -- Wikipedia --

18857.d: This digital artwork is a great example of the benefits that technology has brought to our lives. Technologies such as microscopes, which allows us to see things very small and microscopic have allowed scientists to learn more about the world around them. These techniques have also been used by artists in order to make paintings depicting the world in a different way. With this painting, it's clear that Claude Picasso's message was one of curiosity and life-long learning. It's interesting though, how he uses microscopic cells not just for themselves but for their role in helping us learn more about life and its human significance.  This is of course a very different use to that of the microscope. However, this technique is not just used by scientists but also by many artists during the twentieth century. During this time, there was a development in art techniques that artists called "relief drawing", which involved drawing on a metal plate which could then be magnified to produce micrographs. These micrographs were then normally transferred to another surface (such as paper) so that they could be viewed at an even more microscopic scale. This process was used quite extensively in order to produce accurate representations of life and its processes – especially due to the ability of the relief drawing method and equipment to create accurate detail or magnification.

18893.d:
"Liaisons dangereuses" is a creative exploration of implausible relations between figurative art and poetry. Our AI poet learned on the basis of texts about artists and their work. It memorized all subtleties of a language designed to describe visual emotions and artworks. This language is the tool for creating countless poems about artistic concepts, which range from techniques to materials to artists, etc. But the link is two-sided: if the poet is fed by art language, the concepts expressed by poems do, in turn, influence the appearance of the artwork. Color palettes, pattern types and the flow of the graphic composition are indeed determined by the semantics of the poem.
In each minting, the poet will produce either a short poem (a iambic 5-7-5 haiku  or a iambic cinquain according to Adelaide Crapsey style) or a single verse (either an alexandrine, or a iambic pentameter or an anapestic tetrameter). There are 625 artistic concepts that can trigger a poem, and each concept can generate countless different semantically coherent poems. The poet is completely "unchained": contents might be peaceful harmonic assertions as well as embarrassing, politically incorrect claims.

You can save to file the image by pressing the "s" key.

- Still-Life with Flowers - a generative take on a classic artistic motif.  

The term ‘still-life’ derives from the Dutch word ‘stilleven’, roughly translated it means ‘arrangement of inanimate objects’. Over the centuries, artists have used the ‘still-life genre to try out new techniques and experiment with composition and arrangements. 

- Still-Life with Flowers - is my attempt to (humbly) follow in the footsteps of the artists that contributed to the still life genre and made it into the iconic artistic style it is today.


- Still-Life with Flowers - consists of 256 Flower arrangements (mintable iterations) celebrating compositional experiments and the artistic arrangement of inanimate objects !

For every iteration, over 200 random number generators (fxrand) are triggered to create a unique floral arrangement. (no images were used to create this Artwork)

—

Press R to toggle the animation on / off

Press X to reset 

—

I want to thank everyone who helped me realize this project.
(you know who you are ; )
This project took a long time to make, it was a pretty bumpy road and I could not have done it without your generosity and patience ! 

Made with cables.gl (check it out, it is amazing !)

18913.d:
Minima is a study on focus and color. Playing with the idea of a simple composition of semicircles, either rotated up or down. The focus of the observer is moved with the use of gradual animation in the gradients and occasional circles and/or rectangles connecting the shapes together through color.

The name minima stems from the origins of the composition, mostly taking inspiration from minimalism in its use of a few elements to form a composition greater than the sum of its parts. Less is more, as they say.

The point at the bottom right of the canvas resembles the end of a sentence. Like reading a book, you process the canvas in a similar way, moving from what pops the most to what the least.

As the reader of this canvas I hope you observe what happens to your focus as the colors gradually move across the screen. The animations themselves are looping based on a noised sine wave, which gives them imperfections, imperfections you can observe.

----

Click / Tap on the bar at the bottom of the canvas to open up the GUI, used to export your minima into any format you want. Either .png or .svg. Ready for printing, if you desire.

ps. there might be a secret keyboard shortcut...

----

Minima,
Wouter Missler, 2022,
p5js + webgl.

We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We should move the world to protect animals.

------------------

The giraffe is a large African hoofed mammal belonging to the genus Giraffa. It is the tallest living terrestrial animal and the largest ruminant on Earth. Traditionally, giraffes were thought to be one species, Giraffa camelopardalis, with nine subspecies. Most recently, researchers proposed dividing them into up to eight extant species due to new research into their mitochondrial and nuclear DNA, as well as morphological measurements. Seven other extinct species of Giraffa are known from the fossil record.

The giraffe's chief distinguishing characteristics are its extremely long neck and legs, its horn-like ossicones, and its spotted coat patterns. It is classified under the family Giraffidae, along with its closest extant relative, the okapi. Its scattered range extends from Chad in the north to South Africa in the south, and from Niger in the west to Somalia in the east. Giraffes usually inhabit savannahs and woodlands. Their food source is leaves, fruits, and flowers of woody plants, primarily acacia species, which they browse at heights most other herbivores cannot reach.  -- Wikipedia --

18940.d:
Mountains throughout human history have taken on deep meanings. Coated with immense sacredness by all peoples in the most different places. Being them as a representation of God himself or being the object of worship. For many the mountains were the very abode of the Gods. They are in the collective unconscious as the ability to connect men and gods, through the flow of energy between earth and heaven.

The symbology is very strong. It unconsciously reminds us of the process of encounter between the loneliness of the earth and the hope of the sky, between the fog that blinds and the cloud that supports, between the abyss of the ground and the proximity of the stars. All this is very charming and fascinating.

All human beings have their own mountain, which demands from each one their limits to reach the top, the desire for the breathtaking view, the fear of falling, but also the hope of the last step at the highest point.

In generative art it couldn't be different, going through all the learning, from its fundamentals, to all the countless hours of tests, to countless moments of problem solving and research and more research. This whole process is without a doubt like climbing a mountain. Thinking about the project is exactly like looking at a mountain and imagining how exhausting it will be all the way to conquer it. Finishing your work is like breathing a sigh of relief, looking down and seeing how hard it was to get there, but at the same time looking ahead and realizing how rewarding it was to be able to have that vision and breathe the refreshing breeze of the moment.

After going through a transformation in my first work, where I transmuted my artistic essence from illustration to generative art. Now I come to this second work that I delved into, and after months of climbing this mountain of mine, I give it to you.


- Press "S" in live view mode after loading to save at 1600x1600px.

18971.d:
("Mémoire Vive" aka "Live Memory")

When realtime movement freezes, what you see is just live memory.

Mémoire Vive blurs the frontier between realtime generated animations and unique static images.
A unique random 3D animation is computed in realtime and suddenly it freezes. Then it becomes a unique static evocative picture that won't evolve anymore but that can be zoomed in and snapshot.

WARNING: Webgl/GPU compliant but CPU/mobile should render same static image despite slower. There can be subtle differences between GPU and CPU rendering due to floating approximations.

Mouse/Screen Controls:
- wheel/fingers - zoom
- 2x-click - current window snapshot
- 3x-click - switch to full window rendering

Key Controls:
- H: hide/show help.
- Space - Go further in time.
- I: hide/show info panel. Click for panels (info, FPS).
- A-Q/D - resolution down/up (720p, 1080p, 2K, 4K, 8K)
- S - current window snapshot"
- X - full resolution snapshot
- F - switch to full window rendering
- L - animation loop mode

Mémoire Vive @naibdian 2022 using Opensource WebGL, ThreeJS libs, Inigo Quilez FBM noise functions.

Remix! 
Creativity is a central part of what makes us human. 
Our brains constantly monitor our surroundings, often using them to inspire or direct our creative process. 

Now with technology has come the art of remixing, which is essentially taking one image and altering it to create something new out of it.
That is why I created Geo-Linear.

The colors used in Geo-Linear are all gradients, which in my opinion is much more interesting than individual colors. Eventually I would like to create more pieces of art that follow this style of only having gradients.

"Impression of Rolling Sphere" by UeShiba is a piece that has different interpretations and so many thoughts, ways of seeing it. The artist’s work inspires feelings and emotions from its beauty to the mindfulness of the subject. It is an interesting time as people see life primarily through a different lens.

The gallery explores what it means to have a relation with this painting, how one can perceive it differently, or how they can just appreciate it for what it is: a beautiful piece of art that may give you somatic sensations or even a philosophical thought.

I suggests that this small, sphere is impression of the universe and within ourselves, one can feel the flow of nature, communication between people and with life itself.
